clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read). The national emergency declared in Executive Order 13581 of July 24, 2011, for which this order takes additional steps, was continued by the Presidential notice of July 13, 2026 (91 FR 44727, FR Doc. 2026-14454), which states that it must continue in effect beyond July 24, 2026 and recites this order; the annual notices of July 22, 2019, July 22, 2020, July 7, 2021, July 21, 2022, July 19, 2023, July 16, 2024 and July 21, 2025 (FR Docs. 2019-15794, 2020-16223, 2021-14814, 2022-15973, 2023-15644, 2024-16023, 2025-13929) are also held, one for each year. An OFAC notice (91 FR 63664, FR Doc. 2026-20395, published 2026-10-06) records a designation made on 2026-10-01 under section 1(a)(ii)(A) of Executive Order 13581 as amended by Executive Order 13863, and 31 CFR 590.201 and part 590 in the held eCFR text define amended Executive Order 13581 by reference to this order. The U.S. Code search covers release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09, and the eCFR/CFR search is a point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in the Code edition and none affecting this order is held. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the clause.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13863 of March 15, 2019 (84 FR 10255), Taking Additional Steps to Address the National Emergency With Respect to Significant Transnational Criminal Organizations, has two sections. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13863.txt, 84 FR 10255, PDF pages 1-2) carries the heading, the date March 15, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-05370. Section 1 amends subsection (e) of section 3 of Executive Order 13581 to redefine significant transnational criminal organization as a group of persons that includes one or more foreign persons, engages in or facilitates an ongoing pattern of serious criminal activity involving the jurisdictions of at least two foreign states or one foreign state and the United States, and threatens the national security, foreign policy or economy of the United States. Section 2 contains the rules of construction, implementation and no private right (2(a)(i), 2(a)(ii), 2(b), 2(c)). The dossier inventory (sections 1 and 2 with their paragraphs) covers every operative sentence after the preamble, which is a recital of authority and purpose, so it is accepted. The order states no end. Its force depends on Executive Order 13581 and the emergency it declared, which was continued each July through the notice of July 13, 2026. An OFAC designation of 2026-10-01 applies Executive Order 13581 as amended by this order. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13863 finds the order, the annual continuation notices, OFAC notices and rules describing Executive Order 13581 as amended by it, and 31 CFR part 590; no held text revokes, supersedes or amends it. Executive Order 14294 (the dossier lists it as an unlocated actor) is an order on regulatory criminal penalties and does not name this order. The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for all six clauses. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected.
